title: Restore the original image with one undoable action
summary: Edit > Revert to Original removes editable annotations while keeping the original image intact, with Undo, Redo and normal unsaved-change protection.

Added: Edit > Revert to Original restores the document's embedded source image. One Undo recovers all annotations, and Redo restores the original again.
The shared CLI command revert_original performs the same operation. An empty revert preserves Redo and does not add a history step.
Verified: Native revert, disabled state, Undo/Redo, unsaved replacement cancellation and save/reopen using a seven-object synthetic project.
Native Copy All matches all 256000 source pixels after revert and all 256000 annotated pixels after Undo.
Engine checks preserve transparent RGBA, colored canvas backgrounds, original source data and saved-state tracking.

limitations: This is ClipCraft's independent revert behavior. Broader revert workflows still need verification, so that broader roadmap item remains Needs verification.
Undo history lasts for the current session. Saving a reverted project and reopening it preserves the original image but does not retain removed objects as persistent history.
Pixel grid, snapping, crop/resize, library history and full reference interface parity remain unfinished. Native Save As inspection is still blocked.
